vocabulary.definition: A long upright support that holds a building or platform above the ground or water.
vocabulary.example: Many homes in Ko Panyi stand on stilts above the water.

vocabulary.definition: A place where people establish homes and live together.
vocabulary.example: The settlement developed beside a steep limestone island.

vocabulary.definition: A rock made mainly of calcium carbonate that can slowly dissolve in mildly acidic water.
vocabulary.example: Limestone cliffs give Phang Nga Bay its distinctive shape.

vocabulary.definition: A high, steep face of rock.
vocabulary.example: The cliff rises sharply behind the village roofs.

vocabulary.definition: The regular rise and fall of sea level, caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun.
vocabulary.armenian: մակընթացություն և տեղատվություն՝ ծովի մակարդակի պարբերական բարձրացում ու իջեցում
vocabulary.example: A boat journey through shallow channels depends partly on the tide.

vocabulary.definition: Connected with or affected by the regular rise and fall of sea level.
vocabulary.example: Tidal water moves between the roots of coastal mangroves.

vocabulary.definition: Having only a small distance between the surface and the bottom.
vocabulary.example: A skipper must take care when crossing shallow water.

vocabulary.definition: The coastal area where a river meets the sea and fresh water mixes with salt water.
vocabulary.armenian: գետաբերան՝ գետի և ծովի ջրերի խառնման հատված
vocabulary.example: An estuary connects the river landscape with the sea.

vocabulary.definition: A tree or shrub adapted to growing along tropical coasts in salty or partly salty water.
vocabulary.armenian: մանգրենի՝ աղի կամ աղախառն ջրերում աճող ափամերձ ծառ կամ թուփ
vocabulary.example: A mangrove has special adaptations that help it survive in coastal mud.

vocabulary.definition: Slightly salty because fresh water and seawater have mixed.
vocabulary.example: Brackish water supports a different habitat from a freshwater lake.

vocabulary.definition: Small pieces of rock, sand, mud, or organic material that settle after being carried by water or wind.
vocabulary.example: Moving water can carry sediment into the bay.

vocabulary.definition: To become mixed into a liquid so that the original solid is no longer separate.
vocabulary.example: Mildly acidic rainwater can slowly dissolve limestone.

vocabulary.definition: The gradual wearing away and removal of material by forces such as moving water, wind, or ice.
vocabulary.example: Erosion and chemical weathering can both change a rocky coastline.

vocabulary.definition: Protection from bad weather or danger, or a place that provides it.
vocabulary.example: A protected bay can offer shelter, although conditions still change with the weather.

vocabulary.definition: A relative from an earlier generation, especially one who lived long before you.
vocabulary.example: Stories about ancestors help a community explain its beginnings.

vocabulary.definition: Knowledge and stories passed from person to person by speaking, often across generations.
vocabulary.example: The story of the founding families belongs to the village’s oral tradition.

vocabulary.definition: The work or resources that allow someone to obtain food, housing, and other necessities.
vocabulary.example: Fishing and tourism contribute to local livelihoods.

vocabulary.definition: The traditions, places, and knowledge inherited from earlier generations.
vocabulary.example: A community can protect its heritage while adapting to new opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: A building where Muslims gather for prayer and other religious activities.
vocabulary.example: The mosque is a place of worship within a living community.

vocabulary.definition: Religious prayer or other acts that express devotion to God or a deity.
vocabulary.example: Visitors should respect spaces used for worship.

vocabulary.definition: A structure that extends into water and can provide a place for boats to stop.
vocabulary.example: Before leaving the jetty, we should confirm where to meet the boat again.

vocabulary.definition: A path or passage intended for people to walk along.
vocabulary.example: A narrow walkway connects different parts of the village.

vocabulary.definition: The controlled raising of fish, shellfish, or other water organisms.
vocabulary.example: Aquaculture is one way to produce seafood without catching every animal in the wild.

vocabulary.definition: A seasonal change in winds that often brings a distinct rainy season.
vocabulary.example: The monsoon influences travel conditions along Thailand’s Andaman coast.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to recover from difficulties and adapt when circumstances change.
vocabulary.armenian: դժվարություններից վերականգնվելու և փոփոխություններին հարմարվելու կարողություն
vocabulary.example: Several sources of income can contribute to a community’s resilience.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to find clever, practical solutions to a problem.
vocabulary.example: The football story celebrates the ingenuity of young players with little space.

vocabulary.definition: Put together from available materials to meet an immediate need.
vocabulary.armenian: ձեռքի տակ եղած նյութերով ժամանակավորապես պատրաստված
vocabulary.example: The young players’ makeshift pitch became part of a widely told story.

vocabulary.definition: The upward support that a fluid gives an object, helping it float.
vocabulary.example: A floating platform relies on buoyancy; a stilt building rests on fixed supports.

vocabulary.definition: Existing or happening now, rather than belonging to an earlier time.
vocabulary.example: An older photograph does not confirm the school’s current timetable.

vocabulary.definition: Friendly and generous treatment of guests.
vocabulary.example: We can appreciate hospitality while respecting a host’s privacy.

vocabulary.definition: Not revealing much of the body; used here to describe respectful clothing. “Dress modestly” means to wear such clothing.
vocabulary.example: Modest clothing is appropriate when visiting a place of worship.

vocabulary.definition: Permission freely given by someone who understands what is being requested.
vocabulary.example: Ask for consent before taking a close photograph of a person.

vocabulary.definition: To protect something so that it continues to exist or remains in good condition.
vocabulary.example: Careful tourism can help preserve the places that visitors admire.

vocabulary.definition: Able to be trusted to provide accurate information or work as expected.
vocabulary.example: A reliable account explains which details are documented and which remain uncertain.

vocabulary.definition: A person, document, or other place from which information comes.
vocabulary.example: Compare more than one source before repeating a precise historical date.

vocabulary.definition: A group of people connected by where they live, shared interests, or common responsibilities.
vocabulary.example: Ko Panyi is a community with homes, work, education, and religious life.

quiz.question: Where is Ko Panyi located?
options: On the main island of Phuket
In Phang Nga Bay, in Phang Nga Province
On the Gulf of Thailand coast near Bangkok
Inside a freshwater lake in northern Thailand
quiz.explanation: Ko Panyi is a village in Phang Nga Bay in Phang Nga Province. A tour may begin in Phuket, but that does not place the village on Phuket island.

quiz.question: Why is the distinction between a stilt village and a floating village useful?
options: Stilt houses are moved to a different island every evening.
Floating houses always stand on concrete foundations.
Stilt houses rest on fixed supports; floating structures are supported by buoyancy.
There is no physical difference between the two.
quiz.explanation: Most of Ko Panyi’s buildings stand on supports. The popular description “floating village” can give the mistaken impression that the whole settlement floats.

quiz.question: Which process helps create the limestone karst landscape?
options: Mildly acidic water slowly dissolves limestone.
A new volcano builds every cliff each rainy season.
Seawater turns wooden houses into rock.
Mangrove roots create limestone from salt.
quiz.explanation: Karst develops where soluble rock, including limestone, is gradually dissolved. Erosion and changes in sea level also help shape the broader landscape.

quiz.question: Which description treats the village’s identity most carefully?
options: All people who live beside the Andaman Sea belong to one ethnic group.
Every resident of a stilt village is a sea nomad.
The village is an uninhabited set built for tourists.
Ko Panyi is a settled Thai Muslim community whose identity should not be confused with that of distinct sea nomad peoples.
quiz.explanation: A shared coastal environment does not make different communities identical. Ko Panyi should not automatically be labelled Moken or another sea nomad community.

quiz.question: How should a reader treat the different accounts of Ko Panyi’s founding?
options: Choose the most dramatic version and call every detail proven.
Assume that oral tradition has no cultural value.
Recognize the value of local traditions while acknowledging differences in origins and dates.
Combine all the versions into one exact historical account.
quiz.explanation: Oral traditions can carry meaning and collective memory. When sources disagree, a careful writer identifies the uncertainty instead of inventing certainty.

quiz.question: What practical idea is illustrated by the story of the village’s young football players?
options: Every successful team needs a large stadium before it starts.
People can use ingenuity and cooperation to respond to limited space.
A promotional film proves every historical detail it presents.
Playing on water removes every safety risk.
quiz.explanation: The makeshift-pitch story illustrates an inventive response to a lack of playing space. A dramatized retelling is still different from an independent historical record.

quiz.question: Why do mangroves matter to the surrounding bay?
options: They remove the need for any fishing rules.
They guarantee that storms can never cause damage.
They make every channel deep enough for any boat.
They provide habitat and help connect coastal life with the tidal environment.
quiz.explanation: Mangroves are living coastal habitats, including shelter for young aquatic animals. Their importance does not mean they eliminate every environmental risk.

quiz.question: Which combination best reflects the livelihoods discussed in the story?
options: Fishing, aquaculture, and activities connected with tourism
Only ticket sales for football matches
Only farming on extensive flat fields
Only work in a large factory on the island
quiz.explanation: The village’s economy includes fishing and other seafood activities, as well as restaurants, shops, and services linked to visitors.

quiz.question: What is the most respectful approach to the mosque, school, and residents?
options: Enter every building because the village appears in a tour brochure.
Photograph people first and ask permission afterward.
Follow local guidance, ask before entering or photographing, and avoid disrupting daily activities.
Expect lessons and prayers to stop when a tour group arrives.
quiz.explanation: These are spaces used by a living community. Being welcome as a visitor does not automatically give access to every building or permission to photograph everyone.

quiz.question: Why should a boat visitor check the day’s conditions and return arrangements?
options: The sea level is identical at every time of day.
Weather, tides, and the selected route can affect the journey.
Every tour from Phuket uses the same pier and schedule.
A photograph can provide an exact forecast for tomorrow.
quiz.explanation: A useful plan takes account of real conditions and the operator’s arrangements. General descriptions cannot guarantee a fixed journey time or suitable conditions.

speaking.prompt: Speak for 60–90 seconds as if you were describing a photograph of Ko Panyi to a friend who cannot see it. Describe the position of the cliff, roofs, water, and boats. Distinguish what you can see from what you learned in the article.
speaking.tip: Use “In the foreground…”, “Behind the village…”, “The photograph shows…”, and “According to the article…”. Include cliff, stilts, and shallow. Do not invent details that are absent from the photograph.

speaking.prompt: Give a two-minute explanation of how people can build a settlement where flat land is scarce. Explain the difference between a building on stilts and a floating platform.
speaking.tip: Plan three parts: the challenge, the construction idea, and everyday practical needs. Use “because”, “therefore”, and “whereas”. Try two passive sentences, such as “The buildings are supported by…”

speaking.prompt: Retell the football-pitch story in about two minutes. Explain the problem, the young players’ response, and what the story suggests about cooperation. Finish by explaining why a dramatized film should be read critically.
speaking.tip: Use “At first…”, “They decided to…”, “As a result…”, and “The film presents…”. Include makeshift and ingenuity. Do not add an unverified match result or championship record.

speaking.prompt: Role-play a three-minute conversation between a visitor and a local guide. Ask about the departure pier, the return meeting point, the weather, time in the village, and respectful access to the mosque and school. Then swap roles.
speaking.tip: Use “Could you confirm…?”, “Where should we meet…?”, “Is it possible to…?”, and “Do we need permission…?”. The guide should say “I would need to check” whenever an exact answer is unknown.

speaking.prompt: Speak for two to three minutes about the benefits and pressures that tourism may bring to a small village. Give two possible benefits, two possible pressures, and two practical suggestions.
speaking.tip: Use livelihood, hospitality, preserve, and community. Distinguish a possibility from a verified local fact: “Tourism can…”, “One possible concern is…”, and “I would suggest…”.

speaking.prompt: Compare Ko Panyi with a community or place in Armenia that you know. Speak for two minutes about geography, heritage, hospitality, and how people adapt. End with one question you would respectfully ask a Ko Panyi resident.
speaking.tip: Use “Both places…”, “One difference is…”, and “People have adapted by…”. Compare particular features without assuming that everyone in either community thinks or lives in the same way.

grammar.title: Past simple and present perfect: finished events and connections to now
grammar.explanation: Use the past simple for an event located in a finished past period: subject + past form. Words such as “yesterday” and “in 2011” place the event in a completed time. Use the present perfect for experience without a stated finished time, a recent result relevant now, or a situation that began in the past and continues now: subject + have/has + past participle. “For” introduces a duration; “since” introduces a starting point. Do not normally combine the present perfect with a finished past-time expression: say “The film appeared in 2011”, not “The film has appeared in 2011”. A grammar choice does not make an uncertain historical claim more certain.
examples: The promotional film appeared in 2011. (A finished event with a date.)
Tourism has brought changes to the village. (Past changes connected with the present.)
I visited a coastal village last year. (An invented practice sentence about a finished trip.)
Have you ever visited a village built on stilts? (Life experience; no finished time is specified.)
We have waited at the pier for twenty minutes. (An invented practice situation: we are still waiting.)
We have waited at the pier since nine o’clock. (The starting point of that continuing wait.)
grammar.exercise: Choose the correct form and time word. 1) The film (appeared / has appeared) in 2011. 2) Have you ever (saw / seen) a floating pitch? 3) In this practice situation, we are still waiting: We have waited (for / since) twenty minutes. 4) In the same situation: We have waited (for / since) nine o’clock. 5) I (visited / have visited) the village yesterday.
grammar.answer: 1) appeared — “in 2011” is a finished past time. 2) seen — the present perfect uses the past participle. 3) for — twenty minutes is a duration. 4) since — nine o’clock is a starting point. 5) visited — “yesterday” is a finished past time.

grammar.title: Passive voice: describing buildings, processes, and permissions
grammar.explanation: Use the passive when the thing affected by an action matters more than the person doing it: subject + a form of be + past participle. Present simple passive uses am/is/are; past simple passive uses was/were. A modal passive uses a modal verb + be + past participle, as in “can be reached” or “should be respected”. Add “by” only when naming the doer is useful. Compare “Fixed supports hold the houses above the water” with “The houses are held above the water by fixed supports”. Both describe the same relationship. Passive wording must still be precise: “The village is built on stilts” does not mean every structure has the same construction.
examples: Many houses are supported by stilts. (Present simple passive.)
The practice sentence was written for this lesson. (Past simple passive.)
Limestone can be dissolved by mildly acidic water. (Modal passive.)
Local guidance should be followed. (Modal passive expressing advice.)
Visitors should respect private spaces. → Private spaces should be respected by visitors.
grammar.exercise: Rewrite in the passive. 1) Fixed supports hold many houses above the water. 2) People tell several versions of the founding story. 3) Visitors should respect the residents’ privacy. 4) A writer created this practice exercise.
grammar.answer: 1) Many houses are held above the water by fixed supports. 2) Several versions of the founding story are told. 3) The residents’ privacy should be respected by visitors. 4) This practice exercise was created by a writer. The “by” phrase may be omitted when the doer is not important.
